item.title: The Web I Actually Want
item.description: There are very few pieces of software that I would consider essential, but uBlock is definitely one of them. I’ve been using it for years, and I genuinely love it. For me, browsing the modern web without uBlock feels almost unbearable. Advertisements, trackers, pop-ups, autoplaying videos and countless third-party scripts have become such a normal part of the internet that it’s really easy to forget just how much unnecessary stuff many websites are throwing our way.

item.title: A Small Attempt at Digital Freedom
item.description:
I’ve been thinking lately about the files I create and the formats I use to store them.

On Linux, I’ve always appreciated the feeling of freedom that comes with being able to choose my own path. I can install what I want, configure things the way I like, and use programs that don’t necessarily belong to one particular company or ecosystem.

But I’ve started wondering about something else.

What happens to the files I create?
